mainTopic: Converts and family ties: אין אב לגוי, whether converted maternal brothers may marry each other's wife, trusting a self-serving report, and יונה's prophecies.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question about converted twins. The ברייתא said they are 'not liable' for marrying a brother's wife, and the גמרא explains that this wording only matches the next clause. There is really no איסור at all. רבא then teaches that a non-Jew has no legal father, even when the father is certainly known, and he proves it from twins. Next the גמרא brings two stories as proofs for רב אחא בר יעקב, who says converted maternal brothers have no אשת אח איסור. The first is about ניפטיים הגר, and the second is בן יאסיין's report of רבי עקיבא's ruling. Each proof is turned aside: the first brother may have married the woman while still a גוי, and the ruling was needed only to show that no גזירה was made. The גמרא asks whether the convert in the second story can be believed, and it gives three reasons to trust him. It then discusses רבי עקיבא's other teaching, that the שכינה spoke with יונה only twice. Finally the גמרא begins a new proof from a ברייתא about a convert conceived before his mother converted and born after, and that proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Does 'not liable' mean there is still a prohibition?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא said converted twins are 'not liable' for marrying a brother's wife. That suggests a lesser איסור still exists, which goes against רב אחא בר יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that implies there is still a prohibition!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אחא בר יעקב. It reads the ברייתא's words 'אין חייבין' as hinting that a prohibition still exists, even without a punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Not liable' usually means no punishment, but it can leave room for a rabbinic איסור. If so, the ברייתא fits רב ששת and not רב אחא, who says marrying the brother's wife is completely permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: a prohibition (here, one with no punishment)
they are not liable to punishment
a brother's wife, normally a forbidden relation

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not liable' does not automatically mean 'permitted.' The whole question here is whether the ברייתא meant only 'no punishment' or 'no prohibition at all.'

phrases.english: But there is a prohibition!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אִיסּוּרָא אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the twins ברייתא and the dispute between רב אחא and רב ששת.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's view that there is no prohibition at all
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's wording 'אין חייבין' implies only the punishment is removed, so an איסור remains.

steps.title: The wording only matches the second half
steps.stepSummary: There is really no איסור either. The ברייתא said 'not liable' only to match the next part, which says 'but they are liable.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The same is true that there is no prohibition either. Since the ברייתא wanted to teach in the second half 'but they are liable,' it also taught 'they are not liable' in the first half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אחא. It explains that the words 'not liable' were chosen only to match the style of the second half of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second half of the ברייתא speaks of brothers born after their mother converted. Those brothers really are liable. To keep the two halves parallel, the first half said 'not liable' even though it means there is no איסור at all.

keyTerms.meaning: since / because of the flow of the wording
the first half of a teaching
the second half of a teaching

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common way the גמרא answers: a wording was chosen for style and parallelism, so we should not read extra meaning into it.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ אִיסּוּרָא נָמֵי לֵיכָּא,
phrases.english: The same is true that there is no prohibition either,
and since it wanted to teach in the second half 'but they are liable,'
it also taught in the first half 'they are not liable.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ אִיסּוּרָא נָמֵי לֵיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic parallelism: the wording is explained as matching the other half.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Not liable' was read as 'no punishment, but still forbidden.'
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Not liable' here means there is no איסור at all. The words just mirror 'but they are liable.'

steps.title: רבא: a non-Jew has no legal father, even when he is known
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the rule 'אין אב לגוי.' It is not based on doubt about who the father is. Even a known father does not count legally.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: About what the חכמים said, 'a non-Jew has no father,' do not say this is because they are steeped in immorality, so the father is unknown, but if the father is known we would take him into account. Rather, even when he is known, we do not take him into account.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא makes a new statement explaining the reason behind the rule that a non-Jew has no legal father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could think the rule is only about doubt over who the father is. רבא says no: it is a legal rule. Even a known biological father creates no legal family tie.

keyTerms.meaning: a non-Jew has no legal father
we take into account / are concerned
do not say... rather (rejecting a possible reason)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think 'אין אב לגוי' means the father is just unknown. רבא's whole point is that even a known father does not count legally.
steps.whyThisMatters: This tells us the rule is a legal status, not a doubt. So it applies even in clear cases, like twins.

phrases.english: Rava said: That which the Sages said:
a non-Jew has no father,
do not say it is because they are steeped in immorality,
so that it is not known, but when it is known we are concerned,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ דִּידִיעַ — נָמֵי לָא חָיְישִׁינַן.
phrases.english: rather, even when it is known, we are still not concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, הָא דַּאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side point. It explains the father-side rule that lies behind the twins ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A non-Jew's paternity has no legal weight even when the father is certainly known.

steps.title: Proof from twins who certainly share a father
steps.stepSummary: Twins come from one drop, so their father is certain. Yet the ברייתא's סיפא says twins conceived before their mother converted and born after do no חליצה or יבום. This shows a known father still does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: For two twin brothers come from one drop that split into two, and yet the second half of the ברייתא teaches: they do not do חליצה and they do not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא proves his point from twins, where the shared father is beyond doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule were only about doubt, twins would surely count as paternal brothers and need יבום. Since the ברייתא says no יבום and no חליצה, the father-side tie must be legally erased even when it is certain.

phrases.english: For two twin brothers,
who were one drop that split into two,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא: לֹא חוֹלְצִין וְלֹא מְיַיבְּמִין,
phrases.english: and yet the later part teaches: they do not do חליצה and do not do יבום,
phrases.notes: The סיפא of the twins ברייתא is about twins conceived before their mother converted but born after. They are born Jewish, yet their shared father still doesn't count.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָא שְׁנֵי אַחִין תְּאוֹמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's statement in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that even a known father does not count for a non-Jew
steps.raayaSupportSource: The twins ברייתא: converted twins do no חליצה or יבום.

steps.title: The Torah disowns a non-Jew's offspring
steps.stepSummary: We learn that the Torah treats a non-Jew's offspring as not legally his. The פסוק in יחזקאל compares them to donkeys and horses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: the Merciful One has disowned his offspring, as it is written: 'Whose flesh is the flesh of donkeys and whose seed is the seed of horses.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא draws his conclusion from the twins and backs it up with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father-child bond of a non-Jew is legally cancelled by the Torah. The פסוק compares it to animals, whose offspring have no legal lineage from the father.
steps.whatToRemember: 'אין אב לגוי' is a full legal rule: a non-Jew's father-side lineage does not count, even when the father is certain, as with twins.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: אַפְקוֹרֵי אַפְקְרֵיהּ רַחֲמָנָא לְזַרְעֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Learn from this: the Merciful One has disowned his offspring,
as it is written: 'Whose flesh is the flesh of donkeys
and whose seed is the seed of horses.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: אַפְקוֹרֵי אַפְקְרֵיהּ רַחֲמָנָא לְזַרְעֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the twins proof and adds a פסוק as its source.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The Torah legally cancels a non-Jew's paternity, as shown by the פסוק in יחזקאל.

steps.title: The story of ניפטיים the convert
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the main dispute. It quotes רבי יוסי's story: ניפטיים הגר married his maternal brother's wife, and the חכמים said 'there is no marriage for a convert.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יוסי said: There was a case with ניפטיים the convert, who married the wife of his brother from his mother. The case came before the חכמים, and they said: There is no marriage for a convert.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the dispute between רב אחא and רב ששת. It brings a story as a possible proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים apparently approved of ניפטיים's marriage to his maternal brother's wife. That could support רב אחא, who says there is no איסור. But first the strange wording 'no marriage for a convert' needs explaining.

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rabbi Yosei said:
There was an incident with Niftayim the convert
who married the wife of his brother from his mother,
and the case came before the Sages, and they said:
There is no marriage for a convert.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבא's side point and returns to the רב אחא and רב ששת dispute.
steps.raayaObject: רב אחא בר יעקב's view that maternal brothers who converted may marry each other's wife
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי's story of ניפטיים הגר

steps.title: Can a convert really not marry anyone?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if 'no marriage for a convert' is taken literally, then a convert's קידושין would never work. That cannot be right.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, if a convert gives קידושין, would his קידושין also not take effect on her?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the literal wording of the חכמים's statement, because it leads to an impossible result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Obviously a convert can marry a Jewish woman and his קידושין work. So 'there is no marriage for a convert' cannot mean what it seems to say.

phrases.english: But then, a convert who gives קידושין,

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי לָא תָּפְסִי בַּהּ קִידּוּשִׁין?!
phrases.english: would his קידושין also not take effect on her?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא גֵּר דְּקַדֵּישׁ הָכִי נָמֵי לָא תָּפְסִי בַּהּ קִידּוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the statement in step 6.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Taken literally, a convert could never marry, which is clearly false.

steps.title: Corrected wording: no brother's-wife prohibition for a convert
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording: the חכמים meant 'there is no איסור of אשת אח for a convert.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: There is no prohibition of a brother's wife for a convert.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the statement so it makes sense. The חכמים were saying a convert is not bound by the brother's-wife איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the statement fits the story. ניפטיים was allowed to marry his maternal brother's wife because the אשת אח איסור does not apply to converts.

keyTerms.meaning: the prohibition of a brother's wife

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: אֵין אִסּוּר אֵשֶׁת אָח לַגֵּר.
phrases.english: Rather, say: There is no prohibition of a brother's wife for a convert.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7 by correcting the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A convert has no marriage at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: A convert has no איסור of a brother's wife.

steps.title: Proof that the brother married her as a convert
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that the brother married this woman after he was already a convert. If so, this directly supports רב אחא: no איסור at all between converted maternal brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not that the brother married her when he was already a convert!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof for רב אחא by reading the story as a case where both marriages happened after conversion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first brother married her only after converting, then both brothers were converts during both marriages. The חכמים still allowed it, so there is no איסור, as רב אחא says. 'מאי לאו' means this reading is only proposed, and it can still be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: is it not that...? (proposing a reading as proof)
when he was already a convert

steps.confusionAlert: 'מאי לאו' is a suggested reading, not the final word. The גמרא may still reject it by reading the story differently.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו דְּנַסְבַהּ אַח כְּשֶׁהוּא גֵּר!
phrases.english: Is it not that the brother married her when he was a convert!
phrases.notes: 'The brother' here is her first husband, ניפטיים's brother from the same mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו דְּנַסְבַהּ אַח כְּשֶׁהוּא גֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the corrected wording from step 8 to complete the proof begun in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: רב אחא בר יעקב's view that there is no איסור between converted maternal brothers
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ניפטיים story, read as a case where the first marriage also took place after conversion

steps.title: No, the brother married her while still a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof for רב אחא. It reads ניפטיים הגר's case as one where his brother married the woman before converting.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The case is where the brother married her while he was still a גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 9. It says the brother may have married this woman while he was still a גוי, not after he converted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the brother married her as a גוי, that marriage has no Jewish legal standing once he converts. So there is no real אשת אח problem, and the story proves nothing about two brothers who married as converts. The proof for רב אחא falls away, and the גמרא tries other sources in steps 13 and 26.

keyTerms.meaning: No, that's not the case: the opening of a rejection

steps.confusionAlert: The 'he' in this line is the first brother, the one who married the woman first. It is not the convert who married her later.

phrases.english: No, it is where he married her while he was a non-Jew.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּנַסְבַהּ כְּשֶׁהוּא גּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 9 by offering a different version of the case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof for רב אחא from ניפטיים הגר's case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the brother married her as a גר. He may have married her as a גוי, which is a different case.

steps.title: Why would that case even need saying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the חכמים needed to rule on such an obvious case.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he married her as a גוי, why does this need to be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own answer from Step 10. If the brother married her as a גוי, it seems obvious she is permitted, so why would the חכמים bother ruling on it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A marriage made as a גוי clearly has no אשת אח standing after conversion. A ruling that only teaches something obvious seems pointless. So the new reading of the case looks weak.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? Why does this need to be taught?

phrases.english: While he was a non-Jew? What is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא גּוֹי, מַאי לְמֵימְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading offered in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the brother married her as a גוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that reading is right, the ruling teaches something obvious, which makes it pointless.

steps.title: We might have made a גזירה, so it was needed
steps.stepSummary: The ruling teaches that the חכמים did not forbid the 'married as a גוי' case out of concern for the 'married as a גר' case.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought we should make a גזירה against the 'married as a גוי' case because of the 'married as a גר' case. So it teaches us that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the obvious case still needed saying. Someone might have thought the חכמים forbid it as a safeguard, and the ruling teaches that they did not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fear is that people would mix up a brother who married as a גוי with one who married as a גר. The ruling teaches that there is no such גזירה. The words 'there is no marriage for a convert' now have a real point, and the case of a brother who married as a גר stays unresolved.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said: it introduces a mistaken assumption
Let us make a protective decree
Because of, out of concern for
It teaches us (that this is not so)

phrases.english: You might have said: let us make a decree when he was a non-Jew
because of when he was a convert,
phrases.notes: The worry is that people would confuse the two cases.

phrases.english: so it teaches us that we do not.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: לִיגְזוֹר כְּשֶׁהוּא גּוֹי אַטּוּ כְּשֶׁהוּא גֵּר, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a reason the ruling was needed: to rule out a possible גזירה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have forbidden the 'married as a גוי' case as a safeguard, because of the 'married as a גר' case.
steps.terutzMaskana: No גזירה was made. The ruling covers only the 'married as a גוי' case, so it is no proof for רב אחא.

steps.title: בן יאסיין's story about רבי עקיבא's bench
steps.stepSummary: A new proof: בן יאסיין met a convert overseas who married his maternal brother's wife, relying on רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: בן יאסיין said, 'When I went to the overseas cities, I found a convert who had married his maternal brother's wife. I asked him, "My son, who permitted this to you?" He said, "Here is a woman and her seven sons. On this bench רבי עקיבא sat and said two things. He said a convert may marry his maternal brother's wife. He also said that the פסוק "And the word of ה׳ came to יונה a second time" means the שכינה spoke with him a second time, but not a third time."'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source that seems to support רב אחא. It is a story in which a convert relied on a ruling of רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The convert says רבי עקיבא allowed a convert to marry his maternal brother's wife. The point about יונה is a second, unrelated teaching he heard at the same sitting. It helps show he truly remembers that session.

keyTerms.meaning: Cities by the sea, overseas towns

steps.confusionAlert: The part about יונה has nothing to do with the marriage question. It is simply the second of the 'two things' רבי עקיבא said that day.

phrases.english: Come and hear, for בן יאסיין said:
When I went to the cities overseas,
I found one convert
who had married the wife of his brother from his mother.
I said to him: My son, who permitted you?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי: הֲרֵי אִשָּׁה וְשִׁבְעָה בָּנֶיהָ,
phrases.english: He said to me: Here is a woman and her seven sons,

phrases.aramaic: עַל סַפְסָל זֶה יָשַׁב רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
phrases.english: on this bench רבי עקיבא sat
and said two things:
A convert may marry the wife of his brother from his mother,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר: ״וַיְהִי דְבַר ה׳ אֶל יוֹנָה שֵׁנִית לֵאמֹר״ —
phrases.english: and he said: 'And the word of ה׳ came to יונה a second time, saying':
a second time the שכינה spoke with him,
a third time the שכינה did not speak with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר בֶּן יָאסְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was turned aside, the גמרא brings a second source.
steps.raayaObject: רב אחא's view that converted maternal brothers have no אשת אח איסור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The convert's report that רבי עקיבא allowed a convert to marry his maternal brother's wife.

steps.title: So the brother must have married as a convert
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws its point from the story: the brother married her after converting, which supports רב אחא.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it teaches that a convert may marry his maternal brother's wife. Isn't this where the brother married her when he was already a convert?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls the key line out of the story. It suggests that the brother had already converted when he married the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first brother married her as a גר and the second brother may still marry her, then converted maternal brothers have no אשת אח איסור. That is exactly רב אחא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches: it focuses on the key line
Is it not? It proposes a reading
The wife of his brother from the same mother

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches:
a convert may marry the wife of his brother from his mother.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו, דְּנַסְבַהּ אָחִיו כְּשֶׁהוּא גֵּר?
phrases.english: Is it not where his brother married her when he was a convert?

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי מִיהַת גֵּר נוֹשֵׂא אֵשֶׁת אָחִיו מֵאִמּוֹ. מַאי לָאו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the story in Step 13.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא's ruling, read as being about a brother who married as a גר.

steps.title: Again: the brother married her as a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns aside this proof the same way it did before.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The case is where the brother married her while he was still a גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats its earlier answer. רבי עקיבא's ruling may be about a brother who married her before converting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If so, the marriage loses its standing at conversion, and the ruling says nothing about brothers who married as converts. The proof for רב אחא falls away again.

keyTerms.meaning: While he was still a non-Jew
When he was already a convert: the case under dispute

phrases.english: No, it is where he married her while he was a non-Jew.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּנַסְבַהּ כְּשֶׁהוּא גּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference in Step 14, using the same move as Step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from רבי עקיבא's ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes the brother married her as a גר, when he may have married her as a גוי.

steps.title: Why say something so obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא again asks why the obvious 'married as a גוי' case needed teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does this need to be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats its question from Step 11, now about רבי עקיבא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would רבי עקיבא rule on something so obvious? The question tests whether the new reading of his words holds up.

phrases.english: What is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לְמֵימְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading רבי עקיבא's ruling as being about a brother who married as a גוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Such a ruling would teach nothing new.

steps.title: It rules out a possible גזירה
steps.stepSummary: Same answer as before: the ruling teaches that no גזירה was made because of the 'married as a גר' case.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought we should make a גזירה against the 'married as a גוי' case because of the 'married as a גר' case. So it teaches us that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as in Step 12. The ruling is needed to show there is no protective decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's ruling has a real point even if it is only about the 'married as a גוי' case. So it cannot prove רב אחא's view about brothers who married as converts.

keyTerms.meaning: We should make a decree (another form of לִיגְזוֹר)

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs for רב אחא (ניפטיים הגר and רבי עקיבא) are turned aside the same way. Each may be about a brother who married as a גוי, and the ruling was needed only to rule out a גזירה.

phrases.english: You might have said: we should make a decree when he was a non-Jew
because of when he was a convert,
so it teaches us that we do not.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: נִגְזוֹר כְּשֶׁהוּא גּוֹי אַטּוּ כְּשֶׁהוּא גֵּר, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a reason the ruling was needed: to rule out a possible גזירה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have forbidden the 'married as a גוי' case as a safeguard.
steps.terutzMaskana: No such גזירה exists, so רבי עקיבא's ruling does not prove רב אחא's view.

steps.title: Can the convert even be believed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the convert's report. He quoted a ruling that helped himself, and a ruling quoted after the fact is not accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is he believed? Didn't רבי אבא say in the name of רב הונא, quoting רב: any תלמיד חכם who comes with a halachic ruling is listened to if he said it before the case came up, and not listened to if he did not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the story itself. The convert quoted רבי עקיבא only after he had already married the woman, so maybe we should not trust him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's rule is that a ruling reported after the case has already come up is not accepted. The person may be adjusting it to fit what he already did. Here the convert benefits from his own report, so his quote of רבי עקיבא looks unreliable.

keyTerms.meaning: We listen to him and accept his ruling

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets an important rule about trusting a person's report of a ruling. A ruling quoted before the case came up is accepted, but one quoted afterward, especially when it helps the speaker, is not.

phrases.english: And is he believed?
phrases.notes: 'He' is the convert who quoted רבי עקיבא, and the ruling helps him personally.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn't רבי אבא say that רב הונא said that רב said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁמּוֹרֶה הֲלָכָה וּבָא,
phrases.english: any Torah scholar who rules a halacha and comes forward,
phrases.notes: וּבָא literally means 'and comes.' It's talking about a scholar who brings a ruling to use in a real case.

phrases.aramaic: אִם קוֹדֶם מַעֲשֶׂה אֲמָרָהּ — שׁוֹמְעִין לוֹ,
phrases.english: if he said it before the case happened, we listen to him;
and if not, we do not listen to him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מְהֵימַן, וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the story in Step 13 and questions whether its witness is reliable.
steps.kashyaTarget: The convert's report of רבי עקיבא's ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רב's rule, a ruling quoted after the case has already happened is not accepted. The convert quoted it only after he had married, so his report should not be trusted.

steps.title: He was teaching this ruling before he ever used it
steps.stepSummary: First answer: the convert had been teaching the ruling before the situation came up for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: he had been teaching this ruling all along, and only later did it happen to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 18. The convert was not inventing a ruling after the fact, because he had already been teaching it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern was that a person who reports a ruling only after he has acted on it may be inventing it to protect himself. If he was already teaching it beforehand, he had no personal reason to make it up, so we can trust him.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say (this introduces one possible answer out of several)
He had been teaching it all along (before the case came up)

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
he had been teaching this ruling all along.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: מוֹרֶה וּבָא הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual clarification: the timing of the testimony removes the suspicion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He reported the ruling only after he acted on it, so he should not be believed
steps.terutzMaskana: He had been teaching it beforehand, so there is no suspicion

steps.title: He backed his report with a real case
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: the convert supported his report by pointing to an actual case of a woman and her seven sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: we trust him because he said, 'Here is a woman and her seven sons,' pointing to a real case where this was ruled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the convert is trusted because his report was not a bare claim. He pointed to a known, checkable case, the woman and her seven sons, where רבי עקיבא had ruled this way.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman and her seven sons, a real case where this ruling was given

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
it is because he said:
"Here is a woman and her seven sons."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָאָמַר הֲרֵי אִשָּׁה וְשִׁבְעָה בָּנֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, alternative answer to step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Supporting evidence makes the testimony reliable
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His report is an unsupported claim that helps himself
steps.terutzMaskana: He cited a known case, so his report is believable

steps.title: He reported another unrelated teaching along with it
steps.stepSummary: Third answer: the convert also reported a second, unrelated teaching, which shows he was simply passing on what he heard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: it is different here, because he reported another teaching together with this one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer. Because the convert quoted another teaching of רבי עקיבא together with this one, his report is trusted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other teaching, about יונה, does not help the convert at all. Since he reported both teachings together, it looks like honest transmission and not a story made up to help himself.
steps.whatToRemember: Three reasons the convert was believed: (1) he had been teaching the ruling beforehand, (2) he pointed to a real case, (3) he reported it together with an unrelated teaching.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
here it is different,
because he reported another matter together with it.
phrases.notes: The other matter is רבי עקיבא's teaching about יונה, which the גמרא looks at next.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: שָׁאנֵי הָכָא, דְּקָאָמַר מַעֲשֶׂה אַחֲרִינָא בַּהֲדֵהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, alternative answer to step 18
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A self-serving report given after the fact is not accepted
steps.terutzMaskana: Reporting it along with an unrelated teaching shows he was honestly passing on what he heard

steps.title: The שכינה spoke with יונה a second time but not a third
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back the other teaching the convert reported: the פסוק shows the שכינה spoke with יונה a second time, but not a third time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'The word of ה׳ came to יונה a second time, saying.' A second time the שכינה spoke with him; a third time it did not speak with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the second teaching the convert quoted from רבי עקיבא, about יונה. It is setting up a challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'a second time' (שנית) is read as a limit: there were two prophecies, and no third one. This claim is about to be tested against another פסוק.

phrases.english: The Master said:

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיְהִי דְבַר ה׳ אֶל יוֹנָה שֵׁנִית לֵאמֹר״,
phrases.english: "And the word of ה׳ came to יונה a second time, saying"
a second time the שכינה spoke with him;
a third time it did not speak with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: וַיְהִי דְבַר ה׳ אֶל יוֹנָה שֵׁנִית לֵאמֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the 'other teaching' mentioned in step 21 and looks at it on its own
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From 'a second time' we learn that יונה received prophecy twice and not a third time

steps.title: But a פסוק says יונה prophesied about ירבעם's borders
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this: a פסוק in מלכים says יונה spoke the word of ה׳ about ירבעם restoring Israel's borders.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'He restored the border of Israel from the entrance of Hamath to the Sea of the Arabah, according to the word of ה׳ which He spoke through His servant יונה son of Amittai, the prophet.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the teaching from step 22 using a פסוק that seems to show another prophecy of יונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links ירבעם's conquests to 'the word of ה׳' spoken through יונה. That looks like an extra prophecy, which goes against the claim that there was no third one.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written! (a challenge from a פסוק)
The entrance of Hamath (the northern border)
The Sea of the Arabah (the Dead Sea)

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"He restored the border of Israel
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 14:25. The word in square brackets is added so the line matches the פסוק.

phrases.english: from the entrance of Hamath to the Sea of the Arabah,
according to the word of ה׳ which He spoke

phrases.aramaic: בְּיַד עַבְדּוֹ יוֹנָה בֶן אֲמִתַּי הַנָּבִיא״!
phrases.english: through His servant יונה son of Amittai, the prophet"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כְּתִיב: הוּא הֵשִׁיב אֶת גְּבוּל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the teaching of step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the שכינה did not speak with יונה a third time
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק in מלכים credits יונה with another prophecy, about ירבעם's borders

steps.title: No third prophecy about Nineveh
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the teaching only means there was no third prophecy about Nineveh.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: He was speaking about the matter of Nineveh.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא narrows the teaching: 'not a third time' refers only to prophecies about Nineveh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יונה was told about Nineveh twice and never a third time. A prophecy on a different subject, such as ירבעם's borders, does not contradict this.

keyTerms.meaning: Nineveh, the city יונה was sent to

phrases.english: רבינא said:
He was speaking about the matter of Nineveh.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: עַל עִסְקֵי נִינְוֵה קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Not a third time' means no prophecy at all
steps.terutzMaskana: It means no third prophecy about Nineveh; other prophecies are possible

steps.title: The פסוק compares ירבעם's days to Nineveh's turnaround
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק reads the פסוק differently: it is not a new prophecy but a comparison. Just as Nineveh's fate turned from bad to good, so did Israel's in the days of ירבעם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: This is what the פסוק means by 'according to the word of ה׳ which He spoke through His servant the prophet': just as things turned from bad to good for Nineveh, so in the days of ירבעם בן יואש things turned from bad to good for Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer: the פסוק in מלכים is not describing a new prophecy from יונה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'according to the word of ה׳ through יונה' points back to the Nineveh prophecy as a pattern. Israel's fortune was reversed the same way Nineveh's was, so the teaching stays true even with no limit on its subject.

keyTerms.meaning: ירבעם son of יואש, king of Israel

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers about יונה: רבינא says 'no third time' refers only to Nineveh; רב נחמן בר יצחק says the פסוק in מלכים is a comparison, not a new prophecy.

phrases.english: רב נחמן בר יצחק said,
this is what it means:
"According to the word of ה׳ which He spoke
through His servant the prophet":
just as things turned from bad to good for Nineveh,
so in the days of ירבעם son of יואש
things turned from bad to good for Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative answer to the קשיא of step 23
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק in מלכים records a new prophecy of יונה
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק compares Israel's turnaround to Nineveh's; it is not a new prophecy

steps.title: A ברייתא about a convert conceived before conversion and born after
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the main dispute with a new proof: a ברייתא saying such a convert has ties to his mother's relatives but not to his father's, with examples.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A convert who was born in sanctity but conceived not in sanctity has his mother's relatives but not his father's relatives. How so? If he married his sister from his mother, he must divorce her; from his father, he may stay married. If he married his father's sister from the father's mother, he must divorce her...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the dispute between רב אחא בר יעקב and רב ששת and starts bringing a ברייתא as a proof. The ברייתא continues on the next amud, where the proof is drawn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא deals with exactly the kind of case in the dispute: someone conceived before his mother converted and born after. It rules that only family ties through the mother count for him, and the examples show this: a sister through his mother is forbidden, but a sister only through his father is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: His birth was in sanctity (born after his mother converted)
His conception was not in sanctity (conceived before she converted)
Relatives through the mother / through the father
He must divorce / he may stay married

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A convert whose birth was in sanctity
but whose conception was not in sanctity:
phrases.notes: He means his mother converted while pregnant, so he was born Jewish.

phrases.english: he has relatives through his mother,
but he does not have relatives through his father.
How so?
If he married his sister from his mother, he must divorce her.
If she is his sister from his father, he may stay married.
If he married his father's sister from the father's mother, he must divorce her,

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: גֵּר שֶׁהָיָה לֵידָתוֹ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה וְהוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁלֹּא בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about יונה and returns to the main dispute with a new source
steps.raayaObject: The dispute between רב אחא בר יעקב and רב ששת about converts conceived before conversion and born after
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the family ties of a convert born in sanctity but conceived not in sanctity (it continues on the next amud)
